SpPrAn Configuration Builder

The SpPrAn Configuration Builder is the local browser-based interface in config_builder.html. It can be opened directly or launched from the desktop application.

Important

Files selected in the Configuration Builder are not uploaded to an external service. Representative data files are read locally to identify column names, and folders selected are used locally to obtain filenames.

Choose an analysis mode

SpPrAn begins with a mode-selection view.

Supervised mode

Users define cell types and subtypes directly from protein-marker rules.

Unsupervised mode

Users define major cell types using protein-marker rules, while subtypes are discovered from observed protein-marker patterns.

See Analysis modes for the analytical distinction.

Shared setup

Both workflows require:

  1. a representative .tsv or .csv file, or an existing YAML configuration;

  2. workspace input/output settings; and

  3. primary protein markers.

Settings 1. Restore or start

Loading an existing .yaml/.yml configuration allows users to edit an existing one or take it as a template for a new one.

Selecting a representative .tsv/.csv file allows users to start a new configuration file identifying available positivity columns in their input data.

Important

  • Configuration files from before 0.3.0 are treated as supervised mode configuration files for backward compatibility when restored.

  • Configuration files from before 0.3.0 can be used in the unsupervised mode restoring option. However, it will restore partial information.

Settings 2. Workspace

Specify the input directory, output directory, and common input format. For desktop application users, input and output directory can be selected through the corresponding app.

Important

  • All the files in the input directory must be the same type. If not, SpPrAn will ignore those different from the selected input-file format.

  • Input file names must end with the suffix “_objects.{``filetype``}” to be analyzed by SpPrAn. Otherwise, code will not continue with the analysis.

Note

We strongly recommend to only have the files to be analized inside the input directory and no other non-intented .tsv/.csv file, even if they are inside a folder.

Note

We strongly recommend naming the input files with the suffix “XY_objects.{``filetype``}”, where X and Y are together the “Sample Id” in the analysis. X and Y can be any valid character allowed by the OS. Because “XY” is the Id of the sample, each file must contain different Ids.

Settings 3. Protein markers

Select positivity columns obtained via the representative file to define major populations (cell types). Other protein markers will remain available for other definitions if needed.

Important

The allowed formats for columns in input data to be accepted as “positive columns” are:

  • “Positivity - {protein_marker_name} (MV Cell)”

  • “Positivity - {protein_marker_name}* (MV Cell)”

  • “Positivity - {protein_marker_name} (MV - NUC)”

  • “Positivity - {protein_marker_name}* (MV - NUC)”

  • “Positivity - {protein_marker_name} (MV - CYTO)”

  • “Positivity - {protein_marker_name}* (MV - CYTO)”

Important

When loading an existing configuration file, only protein marker used in the file will appear. Please select a representative file to retrieve and make available all the protein markers you may need.

Note

In unsupervised configuration, user must define a short name for protein markers. The Configuration Builder offers a default name that user can modify. Protein marker short names cannot have the same name between them.

Supervised configuration

In supervised mode, users define:

  • primary cell types and optional hierarchical subtypes using additional protein markers;

  • AnnData saving, overwrite behavior and spatial plotting options.

“Cell types and subtypes” section

In this settings section, users define each major cell type using protein markers that are Present, Absent, or Not applicable, then optionally create nested subtypes using additional markers.

Protein markers selected in settings option 3 will be used to define cell types. Please select introduce a name for the cell type and select the detected intensity signal for the protein markers to define it.

Note

  • Cell types and subtypes’ name can be modified clicking in Edit name button.

  • Cell types and subtypes cannot have the same name or same detected intensity signal for the protein marker definition.

Cell subtypes can be added to each defined cell type by checking the Include cell subtypes checkbox. Cell subtypes will share the same protein markers used for defining the parent cell type. After naming a cell subtype, remaining protein markers can be selected for defining this subtype.

To define a cell subtype from a cell subtype, follow the steps above.

Note

A parent-child relationship represents a nested marker-based phenotype definition, not automatically a developmental lineage. For example:

Immune cells
└── T cells
   └── CD8 T cells

represents nested marker-based phenotype definitions, not by itself a developmental lineage or differentiation trajectory.

Click the Collapse button to temporarily hide the visualization of the cell type or subtype in the webpage. This is especially useful when there are many defined cell types and subtypes.

Other cells will collect all the cells that does not belong to any cell type or subtype. In each parent-child relationship, it can appear Other {parent_name} corresponding to the cells that belong to the parent but no to any of the children.

“Output and spatial plotting” section

In this settings section, users may configure output overwriting, AnnData saving, plot type, DPI, point size, and optional per-sample custom plotting.

  • For Overwrite existing outputs? option, if Yes is selected, previous generated output files in the output path will be replaced by the new ones. If No is selected, SpPrAn will skip generating all the output files that already exist, just creating the non-existent.

  • The AnnData files can be used for generating plots inside and outside this tool, and follow-up analyses outside this tool using Python or R. For Save AnnData files? option, if Yes is selected, AnnData files will be saved in the output path.

  • There are 5 options for plotting spatial plots:

    • Overview: SpPrAn will generate the spatial plots considering all annotations together: in ‘General’ all the cell types in the spatial plot, and all the children for each parent.

    • Highlight: SpPrAn will generate the spatial plots considering a single annotation vs all other cells: if “Immune cells” is a cell type, it will be Immune cells against all non-immune cells.

    • Both: SpPrAn will generate the spatial plots considering the overview and highlight options at the same time. This is the default option.

    • No spatial plotting: SpPrAn won’t generate spatial plots for all samples in the input directory.

    • Custom plotting: SpPrAn will generate custom spatial plot types for each sample in the input directory.

For custom plotting, the builder reads matching filenames from a selected local folder (input folder) and lets the user assign each file an overview, highlight, both, or no plot. After assigning plot types for each file, click Save custom plotting options button for effectively save the assignations.

Important

This is the only option that needs to be saved through clicking a button; every other setting update is automatically saved.

Important

Verify that the corrected input file format is selected before selecting the input folder. If not, you might see no files.

Unsupervised configuration

After defining major cell types, the unsupervised view asks which populations should be explored and which protein markers should define exploratory phenotypes. Discovered phenotypes represent observed combinations of these protein marker states within the selected parent populations.

“Cell types to explore” section

In this settings section, users define each major cell type using protein markers that are Present, Absent, or Not applicable. Cell types also need a short name, that it is used in result and annotation labels.

Note

It is not possible to define nested cell subtypes in this mode.

“Phenotype discovery” section

In this settings section, users choose how broadly SpPrAn should search for protein-marker-defined phenotypes

within the defined cell types.

The Full phenotype discovery option, if checked, discovers protein marker patterns, stores them as subtype definitions, and continues with the supervised workflow. If not checked, SpPrAn will do only the protein-marker-defined phenotype discovery.

The Plot cell-type proportion pie plots? option controls whether sample-level composition pie plots are generated together with the cell-type proportion matrices.

The Overwrite existing outputs? and Save AnnData files? are exactly the same as in the supervised configuration.

“Optional spatial and phenotype analyses” section (New in v0.3.1)

In this settings section, users optionally may choose additional analyses and plots to generate after phenotype discovery.

The Protein marker intensity spatial plots option, if checked, creates one continuous-intensity spatial map per sample and protein marker.

The Neighborhood analysis option, if checked, measures which cell populations tend to be near each other, how frequently they interact, and how their spatial association changes across distance.

Note

The pixel conversion rate can be interpreted as 1:”Pixel conversion rate”. That is because the neighborhood radius supplied to the code is “Neighborhood radius size” / “Pixel conversion rate”. Therefore, if the input data unit is 1:10, consider modify “Pixel conversion rate” to 10 in order to correctly measure the neighborhood radius.

The pixel conversion rate also have an impact in the maximum distance for co-occurrence plot.

The Advanced phenotype classification option, if checked, characterizes previously discovered phenotypes using low, medium, and high protein-intensity levels within each sample. This adds expression-strength information to discovered phenotypes without changing the original positivity-based phenotype definition.

“Group-comparison analysis” section

In this settings section, users optionally assign samples to two groups to compare discovered phenotypes between them. Here, the builder reads matching filenames from a selected local folder (input folder) and lets the user assign each file to each group.

Important

  • If comparison is enabled, both groups must contain samples and use different group labels.

  • Samples may also remain unassigned.

  • Verify that the corrected input file format is selected before selecting the input folder.

“Intensity box-plot data” section

In this settings section, users may select markers whose intensity measurements should be summarized within discovered phenotypes for external downstream boxplot analysis.

“Configuration preview and download” section

Preview the generated configuration in the browser. Download it for use with either the desktop application or in the command line:

sppran --config path/to/config.yaml
